primaryText: ‘Peace!’ said Saruman.
comment: Quotative inversion: the quote precedes the verb and the agent follows it.

primaryText: Le kae? ga botsa Seabelo.
‘Sméagol has to take what’s given to him,’ Gollum answered.
comment: A preposed quote without inversion: the agent stays preverbal.

primaryText: ‘D’oh!’ said the man drunk.
comment: An agent-oriented depictive follows the agent.

primaryText: ‘D’oh!’ said drunk the man.
‘D’oh!’ shouted drunk the man I’ve never met before.
paperFeatures: the man I’ve never met before
comment: Heavy NP shift of the agent lets the depictive precede it.

primaryText: ‘Fire!’ cried Cecil to get the crowd’s attention.
comment: A purpose clause follows the agent.

primaryText: ‘Fire!’ cried to get the crowd’s attention Cecil.
‘Nothing, nothing,’ said Gollum softly.
comment: A manner adverb follows the agent.

primaryText: ‘Nothing, nothing,’ said softly Gollum.
‘Nothing, nothing,’ said Gollum, muttering all about.
comment: An adverbial participial clause follows the agent.

primaryText: ‘Nothing, nothing,’ said muttering all about Gollum.
‘Help!’ tried to yell Alex.
comment: A control complement precedes the agent.

primaryText: ‘Help!’ tried Alex to yell.
‘Where are you going?’ called out John.
comment: A particle precedes the agent; the paper takes (29)–(31) from Collins (2003:4).

primaryText: ‘Where are you going?’ called John out.
comment: The paper takes (29)–(31) from Collins (2003:4).

primaryText: Dumela! go bua Seabelo a tagilwe.
Dumela! go bua a tagilwe Seabelo.
Molelo! go go-ile Seabelo go kopa thuso.
translation: ‘Fire!’ has yelled Seabelo to call for help.

primaryText: Molelo! go go-ile go kopa thuso Seabelo.
translation: ‘Fire!’ has yelled to call for help Seabelo.

primaryText: Titi o molato, go bua kgosi kapela.
translation: ‘Titi is guilty,’ said the chief quickly.
comment: The paper takes (21)–(22) from Collins (1997:2).

primaryText: Titi o molato, go bua kapela kgosi.
translation: ‘Titi is guilty,’ said quickly the chief.
comment: The paper takes (21)–(22) from Collins (1997:2).

primaryText: Ke a go rata, go batla go bua Seabelo.
translation: ‘I love you’ wants to say Seabelo.

primaryText: Ke a go rata, go batla Seabelo go bua.
translation: ‘I love you’ wants Seabelo to say.

primaryText: Mmuu, go bua dikgomo.
comment: The subject marker is the default class 17, not class 10 of the agent.

primaryText: Mmuu, di bua dikgomo.
comment: The starred alternative of (36): the agent’s class 10 marker.

primaryText: Dumela, go bua nna.
Dumela, ke bua nna.
comment: The starred alternative of (38): first person agreement with the agent.

primaryText: ‘Avoid beef,’ advise all the New Age dieticians.
comment: Collins and Branigan’s example and judgments, which the paper reports and disputes with (41).

primaryText: ‘Avoid beef,’ advises all the New Age dieticians.
comment: The starred alternative of (40), Collins and Branigan’s judgment, which the paper rejects (§3.1.2).

primaryText: ‘We should leave,’ thought Max without actually saying __.
comment: The A-moved quotative theme licenses no parasitic gap; the paper takes (62a) from Murphy (2022:4).

primaryText: ‘We should leave,’ Max thought without actually saying __.
comment: The Ā-moved preposed quote of a noninverted clause licenses the gap.

primaryText: ‘Sméagol has to take what’s given to him,’ the Hobbits answer.
comment: Without inversion, agreement must track the agent.

primaryText: ‘Sméagol has to take what’s given to him,’ the Hobbits answers.
comment: The starred alternative of (64).

primaryText: Le kae? Seabelo a botsa.
Le kae? Seabelo ga botsa.
comment: The starred alternative of (65): default agreement without inversion.

primaryText: ‘Where did the wheat go?’ seemed to say the heron.
comment: Subject-to-subject raising of the quotative theme; a corpus example (Flickr) the paper cites from Storment (2025:138).

primaryText: ‘Where did the wheat go?’ seemed the heron to say.
comment: Raising is incompatible with the Ā-moved preposed quote.

primaryText: Dumela, go nna go bua nna.
comment: Aspectual auxiliary raising: both subject markers are the default class 17.

primaryText: Dumela, go bua Seabelo.
Dumela, go a bua Seabelo.
comment: The disjoint morpheme is excluded: the agent stays inside the vP.

primaryText: Said the night wind to the little lamb, ‘Do you hear what I hear?’
comment: The quote itself need not be preverbal: the verb–agent order survives.

primaryText: Ga botsa Seabelo, Le kae?
‘But,’ said Frodo, ‘That is a long way off.’
comment: The quote may split around the verb and the agent.

primaryText: ‘I think that you…’ said Mary, ‘…should go to the store tomorrow.’
comment: The split need not fall at a constituent boundary of the quote.

primaryText: Walked John into the room.
comment: Locative inversion, unlike QI, requires the fronted phrase preverbally.

primaryText: ‘Pop!’ goes the weasel.
comment: A quote need not have internal grammatical structure.

primaryText: ‘Who did a picture of hang on the wall?’ said the professor of linguistics.
comment: A quote need not be grammatical.

primaryText: John warned Mary, ‘There is danger ahead.’
comment: The noninverted clause with a goal DP.

primaryText: ‘There is danger ahead,’ warned Mary John.
comment: A goal DP and the quotative theme cannot both be smuggled.

primaryText: ‘There is danger ahead,’ warned John Mary.
comment: Reversing agent and goal does not help.

primaryText: ‘There is danger ahead,’ warned John to Mary.
comment: A PP goal is licensed inside the PP.

primaryText: Go na le mathaithai kwa pele, go tlhagisitse Neo Thabo.
glossedTokens: Go na le mathaithai kwa pele
translation: ‘There is danger ahead,’ warns to Neo Thabo.

primaryText: Go na le mathaithai kwa pele, go tlhagisitse Thabo a tlhagisa Neo.
glossedTokens: Go na le mathaithai kwa pele
translation: ‘There is danger ahead,’ warned Thabo, warning Neo.
comment: The goal is expressed in an adjunct clause.

primaryText: Into the room walked Mary her dog.
comment: The transitivity constraint holds of locative inversion too.

primaryText: Go et-ela basimane koko.
translation: There are boys visiting the grandmother.
comment: The paper takes (135) from Demuth and Mmusi (1997:14).

primaryText: Kwa maemelong a diterena ga goroga terena.
translation: At the station arrived a train.
comment: Setswana locative inversion with a class 17 locative subject marker.

primaryText: Down from the wall leapt Gimli.
comment: English locative inversion, the paper’s parallel to quotative inversion.

primaryText: Mo kamore-ng go setse go tsene Seabelo.
translation: Into the room already walked Seabelo.
comment: Aspectual auxiliary raising in locative inversion, as in QI.

primaryText: Dikgomo di bua, Mmuu.
comment: Without inversion the subject marker tracks the agent.

primaryText: Dikgomo go bua, Mmuu.
comment: The starred alternative of (35): the default class 17 marker.

primaryText: Nna ke re, Dumela.
Nna go re, Dumela.
comment: The starred alternative of (37).

primaryText: ‘God bless you’ says the men.
comment: Default agreement with a plural agent; a corpus example the paper cites from Storment (2025:139).

primaryText: ‘Giddy up’ says us.
comment: An accusative first person agent with default agreement; a corpus example (Instagram).

primaryText: ‘What do we do now?’ ask we.
comment: Agreement cannot track a first person agent.

primaryText: ‘What do we do now?’ ask us.
comment: Agreement cannot track a first person agent.

primaryText: ‘What?!’ asks the men.
comment: Agree without defective circumvention: default third singular.

primaryText: ‘What?!’ ask the men.
comment: Agree with defective circumvention: agreement with the agent.

primaryText: Go na le mathaithai kwa pele, go tlhagisitse Thabo Neo.
glossedTokens: Go na le mathaithai kwa pele
translation: ‘There is danger ahead,’ warns Thabo to Neo.
comment: Reversing the agent and the goal does not help.

primaryText: Into the room walked her dog Mary.
comment: The transitivity constraint holds of locative inversion too.

primaryText: Mo lefatshe-ng go fula dikgomo.
comment: The paper takes (136b) from Demuth and Mmusi (1997:5).
